title: Long-Term Stable Three-Axis Single-Beam Alignment-Based Atomic Magnetometer Using an Uncoated Buffer-Gas-Free Rubidium Ampoule for Unshielded Geomagnetic Monitoring
abstract: Optically pumped magnetometers achieve exceptional sensitivity, yet sustaining long-term baseline stability in unshielded Earth-field environments (~50,000 nT) remains challenging. We present the design, quantum-interference principles, calibration, and unshielded validation of a three-axis single-beam alignment-based atomic magnetometer built from an unmodified, uncoated, buffer-gas-free commercial rubidium (Rb) ampoule and a single 795 nm VCSEL. Pumped with $45^\circ$-oriented linearly polarized light on the $^{87}$Rb $D_1$ ($F=2 \to F'=1$) transition, the sensor exploits ground-state Zeeman quantum interference (rank-2 spin alignment), intrinsically cancelling first-order vector light shifts. Dual-zone 20 kHz AC heating ($75.0^\circ$C lower liquid Rb reservoir, $85.0^\circ$C upper optical zone) suppresses window condensation and thermal magnetic gradients over 29 days. Without buffer-gas pressure broadening, the VCSEL is stabilized via direct absorption spectroscopy at an optimized 3530 Hz dither frequency, eliminating odd-harmonic intermodulation leakage. A hybrid balanced polarimeter extracts $B_x$, $B_y$, and laser-lock errors from total absorption (sum channel) and $B_z$ from alignment-induced linear dichroism (difference channel) within an active zero-field compensation loop using a 12-bit microcontroller in a dual-stage mid-ranging architecture. Spectral analysis yields sub-LSB noise amplitudes of 0.5-5 pT at 1 Hz (15-150 $\mathrm{pT}/\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$), rolling off to 0.1-1 pT (3-30 $\mathrm{pT}/\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$) near 10 Hz. Continuous unshielded geomagnetic monitoring in Okayama benchmarked against synthesized Kakioka and Kanoya observatory records demonstrates high tracking fidelity and bounds instrumental bias instability to $\le 0.1$ nT at 100-200 s integration times.
